chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father (may the prayers of Allah be upon him) used to say: 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' is a third of the Quran, and 'Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun' is a quarter of the Quran.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Say, He is Allah, One) - Surah 112
key_terms.قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ: Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun (Say, O unbelievers) - Surah 109

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Surah Al-Kafirun according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the immense spiritual weight of these two short surahs, with Imam al-Baqir (AS) attributing to Surah Al-Ikhlas a reward equal to one-third of the Quran and to Surah Al-Kafirun one-quarter. This specific quantification highlights their role as comprehensive summaries of Tawhid and Al-Ma'rifah, serving as essential daily devotions for Shia Muslims to consolidate core theological beliefs.
